2dlabels.purpose: Adds text and arrows directly onto the 2D screen view for figures, annotations, and movies. These labels do not move with the 3D model.
nl_queries: how do I add a label to the view?
2dlabels.notes: Coordinates (xpos, ypos) are relative to the window (0-1). Use `listfonts` to see available fonts. Use backslash escapes like `\\u03b1` for symbols. Example command script: > open > 1bfp; > turn > z 90; > turn > y 10 > preset > pub; > windowsize > 600 400 > 2dlab text 'Blue Fluorescent Protein' color light sea green size 26 x .03 y .92; > wait > 60 > 2dlab #2 ypos .03 size 40 frames 60; > wait > 120 > 2dlab #2 text "here's an arrow" > 2d arrow start .5,.075 end .9,.2 color red; > wait > 120 > 2dlab #2 text 'Fading...' vis f frames 100; 2d arrow #3 vis f frames 100; > wait > 100 See also the G-
2dlabels.related: Distinct from `label` which creates 3D labels attached to atoms/models. Use `color` to change label color. Use `delete` or `close` or `~2dlabels` to remove labels. Use `save` to save the image including the 2D labels.

addcharge.purpose: Assigns partial atomic charges and Amber/GAFF atom types to molecules, often needed for simulations or electrostatic calculations.
nl_queries: how to get charges for simulation?
addcharge.notes: `am1-bcc` is generally more accurate but slower than `gasteiger`. Standard residues (proteins, nucleic acids) get charges from standard libraries. Non-standard residues are parameterized using Antechamber (AM1-BCC or Gasteiger). Check Log for errors. Requires explicit hydrogens (`addh`). The main addcharge command works on both standard and nonstandard residues, guessing net charges for the latter. The subcommand addcharge nonstd allows specifying the desired integral net-charge of an individual nonstandard residue type with name residue-name , for which the atomic partial charges will be calc
addcharge.related: Requires hydrogens, use `addh` first. Often used as part of `dockprep`. Results used by `coulombic` for electrostatic surface coloring. Relies on AmberTools.

addh.purpose: Adds hydrogen atoms to molecular models, considering stereochemistry and potential H-bonds. Also adds missing C-terminal OXT atoms.
addh.notes: Requires existing heavy atoms. Considers H-bonding by default (`hbond true`). Can specify protonation states for specific residues (His, Asp, Glu, Lys, Cys, Tyr) using special names or let the tool determine histidine state based on environment. `inIsolation` controls whether neighboring models influence placement. Hydrogens are added to entire atomic model(s) even if only parts of models are specified. The positions of pre-existing atoms are not changed, but any lone pairs and atoms of unidentifiable element are deleted. Hydrogens are named in accordance with the PDB standard, if possible, an
addh.related: Often used before `addcharge`. Related to `hbonds` for H-bond calculation. Opposite of `delete H`. Part of the `dockprep` workflow. `build` can also add hydrogens in specific modification contexts.

alias.purpose: Creates shortcuts or custom command names that expand into longer or more complex command sequences.
nl_queries: create a shortcut for a command
make an abbreviation for color red target c
how to make a macro command?
alias.notes: Use `$1`, `$2` etc. for arguments within the alias definition. Use `$*` for all remaining arguments. Use `$$` for a literal `$`. Semicolons separate multiple commands within the alias `wordlist`. Saved in sessions and can be added to startup scripts. Within wordlist , $1 , $2 , $3 ... may be used to indicate the first, second, third ... arguments of name . In addition, $$ indicates $ itself, and $* indicates the rest of the line, which allows for variable numbers of arguments. For example, ribbon is aliased to cartoon $* , allowing any of the following to work: > ribbon > ribbon #1/A > ribbon
alias.related: Similar to `functionkey` (assigns commands to keys) and `buttonpanel` (creates GUI buttons for commands). Different from `name` which names selections, not commands. Use `alias list` to see defined aliases, `alias delete` to remove them.

align.purpose: Moves one set of specified atoms (or the model/chain/residue containing them) to structurally align them onto another set of specified reference atoms using least-squares fitting based on coordinate positions.
nl_queries: align structure A onto structure B using these atoms
superimpose these two models based on CA atoms
fit chain A to chain B
calculate RMSD between structures after fitting
align.notes: Requires equal numbers of `matchatoms` and `refatoms` after applying pairing options. `cutoffDistance` allows iterative fitting, removing poorly matching pairs. `move` option controls what gets transformed (atoms, residues, chains, whole structures). `each` allows fitting parts (chains, coordsets) independently. Pairing options (`matchAtomNames`, `matchNumbering`, `matchChainIds`) help restrict which specified atoms are actually used in the fit. Only equal numbers of matchatoms and refatoms can be used in the calculation, but the pairing options may help to restrict broader specifications to o
align.related: Similar to `matchmaker` but `matchmaker` uses sequence alignment first to determine which atoms to pair for fitting, while `align` requires the user to specify the exact atom pairs. `rmsd` calculates RMSD *without* moving structures. `view` can save the aligned position. `fitmap` aligns structures to density maps.

alphafold.purpose: Interacts with AlphaFold services to fetch pre-computed models, predict new structures (monomers or multimers via ColabFold), and analyze prediction confidence (pLDDT, PAE).
nl_queries: fetch alphafold model for uniprot ID
alphafold.notes: `fetch` retrieves from database, `predict` runs new prediction on Colab (requires Google account), `match` finds DB entries similar to open structures, `search` performs BLAST search against AF DB. Predictions have confidence scores (pLDDT in B-factor column, PAE in separate files/plots). High pLDDT (>90) is good, low (<50) is unreliable. PAE assesses inter-residue/inter-domain confidence. Batch commands exist for advanced users running ColabFold locally.
alphafold.related: Similar purpose to `esmfold` (another prediction method). `blastprotein` can search sequence databases including AlphaFold DB. `modeller` is for traditional homology modeling. `alphafold contacts` visualizes PAE on the structure. `alphafold pae` plots the PAE matrix. Fetching is like `open from alphafold`.

altlocs.purpose: Manages alternate locations (alt locs) present in PDB/CIF files, allowing users to view, select, or clean up different conformations of atoms/residues.
altlocs.notes: `list` shows available altlocs and the one currently used. `change` switches the active altloc for a residue and connected atoms. `clean` deletes all but the currently active altloc for specified residues. `show` creates temporary submodels to display multiple altlocs concurrently, `hide` removes these submodels. Altlocs are chosen initially based on occupancy, B-factor, and ID. * altlocs list – list alternate locations and report which is being used * altlocs change – specify which alternate location to use * altlocs clean – delete all but the currently used alternate location * altlocs show/
altlocs.related: `swapaa`/`swapna` might deal with residues that have altlocs. `build` or `dockprep` might precede `altlocs clean`. `attributes` can show altloc IDs.

angle.purpose: Measures or modifies the geometric angle formed by three specified atoms (or points like centroids/markers). Can also measure angles between geometric objects (axes, planes) or angles defined by four atoms (without modification).
nl_queries: measure angle between atom A B C
set angle of atom X Y Z to 109.5
what is the angle formed by these three atoms?
report angle between plane 1 and axis 2
angle.notes: Requires exactly three atoms (or centroids/markers) for measurement or modification. Modification (`angle` value specified) only works if the path between atom 1 and 3 goes through atom 2. `move small` (default) moves the smaller group attached to atom 1 or 3. Can measure, but not set, angles defined by 4 atoms or geometric objects.
angle.related: Related to `distance` (measures distance), `torsion` (measures/modifies dihedral angle - 4 atoms). Part of the `build` structure modification toolkit. Can use geometric objects defined by `define`. `measure` has related subcommands.

aniso.purpose: Displays anisotropic B-factors (atomic displacement parameters) from crystallographic data as thermal ellipsoids around atoms.
aniso.notes: Only works for atoms with ANISOU records in the input file (typically high-resolution structures). Ellipsoid size represents probability (often 50% probability, adjustable with `scale`). Appearance controlled by `aniso style` (color, transparency, smoothing) or `aniso preset`. Works best with stick or wireframe atom styles. Tip : Since the ellipsoids may be obscured when atoms are shown as balls or spheres, using a thin stick representation is recommended (see style and size ).
aniso.related: Uses data (B-factors) often visualized differently using `color bfactor` or `Render by Attribute`. Complementary to `style` and `size` for controlling underlying atom display. `~aniso` hides the ellipsoids.

blastprotein.purpose: Performs a protein BLAST search using a given sequence against various online databases (PDB, nr, UniRef, AlphaFold DB, ESMFold DB) to find similar sequences and associated structures.
nl_queries: find proteins similar to chain A
blastprotein.notes: Requires an internet connection to contact the RBVI BLAST service. Query can be a structure chain, sequence from Sequence Viewer, UniProt ID, or raw sequence text. `database` option specifies which database to search. `matrix` and `cutoff` control search sensitivity/scoring. `showResultsTable` (default true) displays hits interactively. `loadStructures` automatically fetches structures for hits. `showSequenceAlignment` shows alignment in Sequence Viewer. The query sequence can be given as any of the following: * a chain-spec corresponding to a single chain in an atomic structure open in Chimer
blastprotein.related: `alphafold search` and `esmfold search` are specialized searches within those specific databases. `similarstructures blast` uses BLAST as part of structure-based similarity searching (Foldseek). `matchmaker` aligns structures based on sequence alignment. Results can be viewed in the Sequence Viewer. Fetched structures are opened like with the `open` command.

bond.purpose: Creates or deletes covalent bonds between specified atoms, or modifies the length of an existing bond.
nl_queries: add a bond between atom A and atom B
delete the bond between these atoms
bond.notes: `bond atom-spec` adds bonds. `reasonable true` (default) only adds bonds if atoms are close; `reasonable false` adds them regardless of distance. `~bond atom-spec` deletes bonds between specified atoms. `bond length atom-spec [length]` sets or reports bond length (requires exactly two atoms forming an existing bond). `move small` (default) moves the smaller fragment when changing length. Atoms must be in the same model to be bonded (`combine` models first if needed). A bond can only be added between atoms that are in the same atomic model; if they are in separate models, a single combined mode
bond.related: `build` uses bonding implicitly. `angle` and `torsion` act on angles defined by bonds. `pbond` manages pseudobonds (non-covalent connections). `combine` merges models without necessarily adding bonds between them. `delete sel` can delete selected bonds.

build.purpose: Provides tools for building and modifying atomic structures, including starting new molecules (atoms, fragments, peptides, nucleic acids), modifying existing atoms, joining models, inverting stereocenters, and replacing chain segments.
nl_queries: join model 1 and model 2 with a bond
build.notes: `start` creates new, separate models. `modify` changes atom type, adds hydrogens based on geometry. `join` merges two models with a new covalent bond (peptide or generic), deleting/replacing specified atoms. `invert` swaps two substituents of a central atom. `replace` copies coordinates from one chain segment to another (no fitting involved). Building actions are generally not undoable, save sessions often. • build start atom model-info [ position x,y,z ] [ resName resname ] [ select true | false ] • build start fragment model-info fragment-name [ position x,y,z ] [ resName resname ] • build s
build.related: Uses `bond`, `angle`, `torsion` implicitly or explicitly. `addh` adds hydrogens more globally. `delete` removes atoms/bonds. `swapaa`/`swapna` replace sidechains/bases with rotamers. `combine` merges models without bonding. `open` can build structures from SMILES. `rna` builds RNA helices.

bumps.purpose: Identifies and marks protrusions (bumps) on an isosurface relative to a central point, primarily designed for analyzing cell surface features in microscopy volume data.
bumps.notes: Requires a `volume` model and a `center` point (usually a marker model). Parameters `range`, `baseArea`, and `height` control the detection algorithm sensitivity. `bumps report` provides statistics on detected bumps (size, height, signal from another map). Finds radially oriented protrusions best. Examples: > bumps #1 center #2 height 1 base 100 range 75 > bumps report #3 save ~/Desktop/prot.txt signalMap #4 Conceptually, rays are followed out from the center up to the range distance, and distance maxima in the isosurface are identified. The rays for maxima are followed back toward the center
bumps.related: Operates on `volume` data and its isosurface. Uses `marker` models for input (center) and output (bumps). `measure convexity` provides a different measure of surface shape.

buttonpanel.purpose: Creates custom graphical panels containing buttons that execute specified ChimeraX commands when clicked.
nl_queries: add a button to run a command
buttonpanel.notes: First command defines the panel title and layout (rows, columns). Subsequent `add` commands add buttons with a name and the command string to execute. Commands with spaces need quotes. Panel layout fills row-wise or column-wise. If the number of rows N and columns M in the panel is not given, all of the buttons will be placed in a single row. Each use of add creates an additional button with text button-name that executes button-command when clicked. Each button-command may be a composite of other commands, i.e. , multiple commands separated by semicolons, and should be enclosed in quotation m
buttonpanel.related: Similar to `alias` (creates command shortcuts) and `functionkey` (assigns commands to keys), but provides a graphical interface. Panels can be specified for use with `vr` command's `gui` option. Commands executed can use `sel` or other dynamic specifiers. Saved in sessions.

camera.purpose: Controls the viewing mode (mono, stereo, orthographic, 360, dome) and parameters related to stereo vision (eye separation, field of view, convergence).
camera.notes: `mode mono` is default perspective. `mode ortho` removes perspective. `mode crosseye`/`walleye`/`sbs`/`tb` are for stereo. `mode stereo` requires specific hardware. `mode 360`/`dome` are special projections. `eyeSeparation`, `fieldOfView`, `convergence` fine-tune stereo/viewing. Running `camera` with no arguments reports current settings. The camera mode can be: * mono (default) – monoscopic with perspective (apparent size decreasing with distance from the viewer) * ortho – orthographic, monoscopic without perspective * crosseye – side-by-side left- and right-eye views for visualization with c
camera.related: Complements `view` (which controls camera position/orientation) and `zoom` (which controls magnification/scale). `vr` command manages camera settings specifically for virtual reality. Settings affect image saving via `save`. `getcrd` reports camera position.

cartoon.purpose: Show or hide cartoon/ribbon backbone representation; set cartoon style.

cd.purpose: Changes the current working directory for file operations within ChimeraX.
cd.notes: `cd` with no argument goes to the home directory. `cd browse` opens a file browser. Directory paths are standard OS paths. Running a command file temporarily changes `cd` to that file's location.
cd.related: Affects default paths for `open` and `save`. `pwd` reports the current directory. `runscript` temporarily changes the directory while executing a script.

changechains.purpose: Changes the chain identifiers (chain IDs) of specified residues or atoms. Can also standardize glycosylation chain IDs to match the protein chain they are attached to.
nl_queries: change chain A to chain B
set chain ID for these residues to X
changechains.notes: Can change specified atoms/residues to a single `new-ID`, or change multiple IDs based on paired lists (`current-ID-list` to `new-ID-list`). `changechains glycosylations` automatically finds and re-ID's HET chains bonded to specified biopolymer chains. Chain IDs are case-sensitive. Either a single desired chain ID can be given, or a comma-separated list of current IDs followed by a comma-separated list of the desired IDs. If lists are used, they must contain equal numbers of IDs, which will be paired in the order given. Ranges of IDs cannot be given. Within the set of specified atoms, occurren
changechains.related: Related to `rename` (changes model names) and `renumber` (changes residue numbers). `combine` and `build join` might necessitate chain ID changes to avoid conflicts. `save` writes the modified chain IDs to output files.

clashes.purpose: Find and show steric clashes between atoms.

clip.purpose: Controls near/far and front/back clipping planes to hide parts of the scene or reveal interiors.
nl_queries: show a slice through the model
slab the view near this atom
turn off clipping for the surface
clip.notes: `near`/`far` planes are parallel to the screen. `front`/`back` planes move with the model and can be oriented arbitrarily (`axis`). `offset` values move planes relative to a `position` (default center) or current location. `clip off` or `~clip` disables all clipping. `clip model` allows clipping specific models differently (only for front/back planes). Each plane can be activated or turned off individually; specifying an offset activates a plane if it was not already active. Offsets are in physical distance units (generally Å), with positive values increasing away from the viewer for the near/
clip.related: `surface cap` controls appearance of clipped surfaces. Mouse modes allow interactive clipping. `view` saves clipping plane status. `cofr` (center of rotation) is often used as the reference point. `perframe` can animate clipping.

close.purpose: Removes models (structures, maps, surfaces, etc.) or the entire session from ChimeraX.
close.notes: `close` with no arguments closes all models. `close #N` closes model N and its submodels. `close session` clears all data and resets many global settings. Closed models cannot be recovered except by reopening or reloading a saved session. Examples: > close > close #1 > close #2,4-6 > close #3.2 > close #3.2-10
close.related: Opposite of `open`. `hide` makes models invisible but doesn't remove them. `delete` removes atoms/bonds within a model, not the whole model. `quit` exits ChimeraX entirely.

cofr.purpose: Sets or reports the center of rotation (CoR) for mouse-controlled scene manipulation.
nl_queries: set center of rotation to this atom
where is the center of rotation?
cofr.notes: `frontCenter` (also `~cofr`) updates CoR based on view/front objects (default-like behavior). `centerOfView` updates based on window center and clipping planes. `fixed` uses the last defined point. Can specify a point explicitly using coordinates or `spec` (center of specified items). `showPivot` displays a visual marker for the CoR. The first set of options specify the center of rotation method : * frontCenter – use the front center method (also specified with ~cofr ): when the view is zoomed out, use the center of the bounding box of all displayed items; when the view is zoomed in, keep upda
cofr.related: Affects `mousemode` rotation behavior. `view` saves/restores the CoR method and position. `measure center` calculates geometric centers which can be used as input for `cofr`. `move cofr` translates the scene relative to the CoR.

color.purpose: Colors various items (atoms, bonds, cartoons, surfaces, labels, maps) using specified colors, built-in schemes (by element, chain, residue type), sequential schemes (rainbow), or based on attribute values, map values, or distance. Also manages named colors.
nl_queries: color surface based on map values
color.notes: `target` option specifies what part is colored (atoms `a`, bonds `b`, cartoon `c`, surface `s`, pseudobonds `p`, ring fill `f`, labels `l`). `color byelement`, `bychain`, `byidentity`, `bymodel`, `random`, `bynucleotide` are built-in schemes. `color sequential` (`rainbow`) applies colors along chains/models. `color byattribute` is very versatile. Palettes (`palette` option) define color ranges for value-based or sequential coloring. Color names, hex codes, or rgb values can be used. `color modify` changes existing colors. Additional subcommands manage the set of named colors: * color name – de
color.related: `transparency` sets transparency. `coulombic` and `mlp` color surfaces by electrostatic potential. `surface` and `volume` create objects that can be colored. `cartoon` uses default coloring schemes. `key` or `Color Key` tool creates a legend for value-based coloring. `rainbow` is a synonym for `color sequential`. `preset` can use color commands. `Render by Attribute` tool provides GUI for attribut

combine.purpose: Merges multiple atomic models into a single new model, or copies a single atomic model. Coordinates are preserved; no new bonds are automatically formed between the merged parts unless `retainIds true` causes residues to become sequential.
combine.notes: Does not move models relative to each other. `close true` removes original models. `modelId` and `name` specify properties of the new combined model. `retainIds false` (default) reassigns duplicate chain IDs; `retainIds true` keeps original IDs but fails if residue number conflicts arise; it may also implicitly form bonds/pseudobonds between chains with the same ID if residue numbering allows. By default ( retainIds false ), duplicate chain IDs are resolved by assigning new chain IDs. Giving retainIds true indicates instead keeping all chain IDs the same as in the original models, as long as d
combine.related: Different from `build join` which forms a covalent bond and repositions atoms. `split` does the opposite (separates chains/models). `mcopy` copies models while applying transformations. `save` can save the combined model. Chain IDs might need adjustment using `changechains` or `renumber` afterwards.

coordset.purpose: Play or step through trajectory frames / coordinate sets.

coulombic.purpose: Calculates and displays Coulombic electrostatic potential (ESP) on molecular surfaces to show charge distribution.
coulombic.notes: Default colors are red (negative) to white (zero) to blue (positive). Calculation uses a distance-dependent dielectric model by default (`distDep true`). Requires atomic partial charges (looks up standard, calculates non-standard via Antechamber unless already present). `offset` shifts calculation relative to surface (1.4A often used for outer surfaces, 0 for planar caps). `key true` automatically adds a color key. The calculation can handle structures with or without explicit hydrogens ( details... ). Partial atomic charges are looked up for standard residues, and in the rarer case they are n
coulombic.related: Uses atomic charges, often assigned previously with `addcharge` (or calculates them on the fly). `mlp` calculates potential using a lipophilicity approach. `surface` creates the surface to be colored. `key` (via `coulombic ... key true` or separately) creates a legend. Uses palettes for coloring (default red-white-blue). `color` can also color surfaces by map values (if ESP is saved as a map, thou

crossfade.purpose: Smoothly fade between two views or displays (for movies).

crosslinks.purpose: Modifies the appearance (radius, dashes, color) of pseudobonds, often used for visualizing crosslinking or other distance restraint data. Also provides tools to analyze these pseudobonds (histogram, network diagram, length minimization).
crosslinks.notes: The top-level command changes display style. Subcommands `histogram`, `network`, `minimize` perform analyses. `histogram` plots length distribution. `network` shows inter-chain links. `minimize` moves specified models (`moveModels`) as rigid bodies to shorten inter-model pseudobonds. The top-level command sets pseudobond stick radius , number of dashes N , and/or color . Only whole numbers of dashes are accepted, with 0 indicating solid sticks. Currently, odd numbers are rounded down to give an even number of dashes. The following subcommands perform plotting and other analyses: * crosslinks h
crosslinks.related: Acts on pseudobonds, created by `pbond` or loaded from files (e.g., IHM mmCIF). `clashes`/`contacts` find close contacts, `hbonds` finds hydrogen bonds (also pseudobonds). `distance` measures distances. `label` can label pseudobonds.

crystalcontacts.purpose: Identifies and analyzes close contacts between symmetry-related copies of a molecule in a crystal lattice.
nl_queries: show neighboring molecules in the crystal
calculate buried area at packing interface
crystalcontacts.notes: Requires symmetry information (e.g., from PDB/CIF header). `distance` defines contact threshold. `copies true` loads full atomic copies. `schematic true` shows a simplified marker representation. `residueInfo` logs residue pairs in contact. `buriedAreas` calculates and logs buried SASA at the contact interface. One or more atomic models can be specified . Any atoms one wishes to exclude from the calculation (solvent, etc. ) should be deleted beforehand. Symmetry copies can be shown as full atomic models and/or represented schematically . Results are reported in the Log ( details... ).
crystalcontacts.related: Uses symmetry information often visualized with `unitcell` and `sym`. Related to `clashes`/`contacts` (which find contacts within or between arbitrary models, not necessarily symmetry-related). `interfaces` calculates properties of interfaces between chains/models.

define.purpose: Defines geometric objects (axes, planes, centroids) based on specified atoms, points, or other geometric objects.
define.notes: `axis` can be defined by atoms/points, per helix, from two points, or normal to a plane. `centroid` can be mass-weighted. `plane` defines a best-fit plane. Options control appearance (color, radius, length, padding), naming (`name`, `id`), and calculation details (mass-weighting, which eigenvector for axes). Objects are created as separate models. > Axes can be defined: > by a set of at least two specified atoms ( > perHelix > false), where > markers > such as from > define centroid > are equivalent to atoms > for each protein helix in models containing the specified atoms ( > perHelix > true)
define.related: Objects created can be used in `distance` and `angle` measurements, or to orient the `view`. `measure inertia` calculates inertia properties without creating persistent objects. `aniso` visualizes anisotropic B-factors (related to thermal ellipsoids, not inertia). `shape` creates basic geometric shapes unrelated to atoms. `marker` can create points, similar to `define centroid`.

delete.purpose: Permanently removes specified atoms, bonds, or pseudobonds from their models.
nl_queries: delete the bond between atom A and B
delete.notes: Default is `delete atoms`. Specify `bonds` or `pseudobonds` explicitly. `attachedHyds true` (default) also deletes hydrogens bonded to deleted heavy atoms. Deletion is permanent within the session (cannot be undone except by reopening/reloading).
delete.related: Different from `hide` (makes items invisible but doesn't remove them) and `close` (removes entire models). `~bond` also deletes bonds. `addh` adds hydrogens, `delete H` removes them. `build` involves adding/deleting atoms/bonds.

devel.purpose: Provides tools for developers to build, install, and manage ChimeraX bundles (plugins/extensions).
nl_queries: how to develop a chimerax extension
devel.notes: This command is primarily for ChimeraX developers. It includes subcommands: `alias`/`unalias` (manage path shortcuts), `build` (compile/prepare bundle), `clean` (remove build files), `dump` (log metadata), `install` (install bundle, optionally user-specific or editable), `pip` (manage Python packages). > Assign a convenient > name > to a > path > on the system, for use in other > devel > commands. If no arguments are given, list all of the currently defined path aliases. If > name > but not > path > is given, report the path aliased to that name. If a new path is entered for a name already in
devel.related: `pip` is closely related (and `devel pip` is a synonym). General development might involve scripting using commands like `runscript`.

distance.purpose: Measures the distance between two specified objects (atoms, axes, planes) and optionally creates a persistent, labeled pseudobond (distance monitor) for atom-atom distances.
nl_queries: measure distance between atom X and atom Y
show the distance from this atom to the plane
what is the distance between these two atoms?
distance.notes: Creates persistent, dynamically updating "distance monitors" (pseudobonds) only for atom-atom distances by default (`monitor true`). Distances involving axes/planes are reported but not monitored. `distance delete` or `~distance` removes monitors. `distance style` modifies monitor appearance and defaults. `distance save` outputs measurements to a file. In the case of two atoms, unless monitor false is given, a distance monitor pseudobond (see also the Distances graphical interface) is added and labeled according to the display options . Although subsequent changes in distance are not logged, d
distance.related: Complementary to `angle` for geometric measurements. Uses `axis` and `plane` objects created by `define`. Distance monitors are a type of `pseudobond`, styled with commands like `pbond`, `color`, `style`, `size`, `label`. Related to commands that find specific distance-based relationships like `clashes`/`contacts`, `hbonds`, `crosslinks`. `getcrd` reports coordinates, which distances are based on.

dockprep.purpose: Prepares molecular structures (usually proteins and ligands) for docking or other computational procedures by performing a series of common cleanup and preparation steps.
nl_queries: add hydrogens and charges to protein
use Dunbrack library to complete sidechains
dockprep.notes: Provides a streamlined workflow for common structure preparation tasks. Options allow toggling specific steps (delete solvent/ions/altlocs, add hydrogens, add charges, standardize residues) and choosing methods (rotamer library for sidechains, charge calculation method). Settings can be saved/reused with `memorize`. Hydrogen addition options (`ah...`) mirror those in `addh`. > delAltLocs > true > | false > Whether to delete all but the currently used alternate locations (default > true > ). See also: > altlocs clean > completeSideChains > method > Whether and how to repair truncated amino acid
dockprep.related: A convenience command that combines functionality from `delete` (solvent/ions/altlocs), `swapaa` (or rotamer libraries for `completeSideChains`), `addh` (adding hydrogens), and `addcharge` (adding charges). `altlocs clean` is related to `delAltLocs`.

exit.notes: `exit` and `quit` are synonyms. This command closes the entire application, potentially losing unsaved work if not prompted.
exit.related: `close` closes models or the entire session data but doesn't terminate the application itself. `stop` halts command execution, not the application.

fitmap.purpose: Fit atomic models or maps into density maps.

fly.purpose: Animate the camera through a series of saved views.

getcrd.purpose: Reports the X,Y,Z coordinates of specified atoms in the Log.
nl_queries: what are the coordinates for atom X?
getcrd.notes: Output goes to the Log. Can specify coordinate system: `model` (original), `scene` (default, accounts for relative model movements), or `screen` (2D projection plus depth). `model` and `scene` are identical if models haven't been moved relative to each other. The keywords indicate which coordinate system to use: * model - the original coordinate system of a model * scene (default) - the scene coordinate system , which includes changes from moving any models relative to other models (by fitting, matching, etc. ) * screen - the screen coordinate system , with X horizontal increasing rightward, Y
getcrd.related: Coordinates are the basis for geometric calculations like `distance` and `angle`. `save PDB` writes model coordinates to a file. `camera` and `view` relate to the scene and screen coordinate systems. `Map Coordinates` tool relates atomic and map coordinates.

wait.purpose: Pauses command script execution for a specified number of display frames. Allows multi-frame commands (like rotations or translations) to complete before the next command starts. Can also be used to insert pauses or duplicate frames in movies.
wait.notes: Takes an optional integer `wait-frames`. If omitted, it automatically waits for specific preceding commands (`move`, `turn`, etc.). windowsize.purpose: Sets the size (width and optionally height) of the main ChimeraX graphics window in pixels. Also reports the current size if run without arguments.
windowsize.notes: Takes optional `width` and `height` in pixels. If only `width` is given, height remains unchanged. No arguments reports current dimensions to status bar and Log. Affects default output resolution for images/movies. Whether to restore the graphics window size when restoring a session is set in the Window preferences . See also: save image , movie , view , making images , making movies , ChimeraX window
windowsize.related: `windowsize` sets the dimensions of the graphics window. This size is then used as the default by `save image` and `movie` recording unless overridden by options within those commands. `view` adjusts the camera framing within the window but doesn't change the window size itself. Window preferences control whether this size is restored with sessions.

wobble.purpose: Rotates models or the entire scene in a continuous figure-eight (infinity symbol) motion around a specified axis and center.
wobble.notes: Takes `axis` (default y), `angle` amplitude (default 30°), `frames` (default forever), `cycle` frames per figure-eight (default 136), `aspect` ratio (minor/major rotation amplitude, default 0.3). `center` and `coordinateSystem` options define the rotation point/frame. Can rotate specific `models`/`atoms` or the whole scene (default). Use `stop` to halt the default infinite motion. Atom movements are not undoable. Commands continue to be processed while the requested motion is in progress. To pause command processing until the motion is finished, use the wait command.
wobble.related: `wobble` is a specialized rotation command. `turn` and `roll` can replicate the wobble motion using their `wobble` and `wobbleAspect` options, but `wobble` has different defaults. `rock` performs a back-and-forth rocking motion. `stop` halts ongoing `wobble` motion. `wait` pauses script execution until a specified number of wobble frames complete (if `frames` was specified). `cofr`, `move`, `zoom`

zone.notes: Operates around a *single* specified residue. Hides non-zone atoms/labels, optionally shows distant parts as a narrow ribbon (`ribbons true` default). Restricts volume display based on `surfaceDistance`. Cutoff distances persist until changed. `zone clear` restores the previous display state. `zone setting` adjusts label colors/backgrounds. zoom.purpose: Adjusts the magnification (zoom level) of the view, making objects appear larger or smaller. Can zoom by a relative factor or set an absolute scale (pixel size).
zoom.notes: Zooms by `factor` ( >1 enlarge, <1 shrink) relative to current view, or sets absolute `pixelSize` (length units per pixel at center of rotation). Can occur over multiple `frames`. No arguments reports current pixel size at center of rotation. Moves the camera, does not change model coordinates. Adjusts active clipping planes. The zoom command moves the camera toward or away from the scene. It does not change model coordinates.
zoom.related: `zoom` changes the camera's distance/magnification. `view` can also adjust zoom level as part of focusing on objects. `camera` controls other camera parameters like mode (perspective/orthographic). `scalebar` displays a bar indicating the current scale. `mousemode` allows interactive zooming. `turn`, `roll`, `move` perform other view transformations.
